question: What is the purpose of the avionics ventilation system?

options.text: To supply fresh air to the passengers
To pressurise the cargo hold
To cool the electronic equipment in the avionics bay and the cockpit panels, and to remove smoke from them
To heat the electronic equipment compartment in cold weather only

explanation: Avionics generate heat and are sensitive to temperature. The system circulates air through the avionics bay and cockpit instrument panels and extracts it overboard.

question: Which two fans are part of the avionics ventilation system?

options.text: A blower fan and an extract fan
A recirculation fan and a pack fan
A cargo fan and a lavatory fan
An inlet fan and a diffuser fan

explanation: The blower fan pushes air into the system and the extract fan draws it out. A fault in either one is shown by a light on the overhead panel.

question: Which unit decides the configuration of the avionics ventilation system automatically?

options.text: The cabin pressure controller
The zone controller
The flight warning computer
The avionics equipment ventilation computer (AEVC)

explanation: The AEVC selects the valve positions and fan operation according to ground/flight status and skin temperature, and monitors for smoke.

question: Which configurations does the avionics ventilation system have?

options.text: A summer and a winter configuration only
An open circuit, a closed circuit, an intermediate configuration and a smoke configuration
An economy and a high-flow configuration
A ground and a flight configuration only

explanation: The configurations are selected automatically according to temperature and ground/flight conditions, and the smoke configuration overrides the others.

question: What happens to the avionics ventilation in the smoke configuration?

options.text: The blower and extract fans stop
Air is not recirculated and is extracted overboard, with fresh cabin air as the source
The system is reconfigured to recirculate all the air
The avionics are depressurised

explanation: In the smoke configuration the system draws in conditioned air and extracts the smoke directly overboard, with no recirculation, so that smoke is cleared from the avionics bay.

question: What does the skin heat exchanger do in the closed circuit configuration?

options.text: It heats the cargo hold
It cools the pack bleed air
It warms the cabin air
It cools the avionics ventilation air using the cold of the fuselage skin

explanation: In flight the outer skin is cold. In closed circuit the air passes alongside the skin and gives up its heat, with no air taken from or sent to the cabin.

question: Which light on the overhead panel shows a fault in the avionics ventilation blower fan?

options.text: The BLOWER FAULT light
The EXTRACT FAULT light only
The CAB FANS FAULT light
The RAM AIR light

explanation: There are separate BLOWER and EXTRACT lights on the VENTILATION panel. Each one comes on, amber, when its fan has a fault or is overheating.

question: What is the effect of the CAB FANS pushbutton?

options.text: It starts or stops the avionics blower fan
It opens or closes the outflow valve
It starts or stops the cabin recirculation fans
It starts or stops the lavatory extract fan

explanation: The pushbutton is on the air conditioning panel. The avionics fans are automatic, with only an override on the ventilation panel.

question: How is the air from the lavatories and galleys removed from the cabin?

options.text: By the recirculation fans
By the avionics extract fan
By the packs
By an extraction fan, and the air is discharged overboard through the outflow valve area

explanation: The extraction system prevents odours spreading in the cabin and keeps the lavatory at a slightly lower pressure than the cabin.

question: What is the effect on cargo compartment ventilation if the isolation valves are closed?

options.text: The cargo compartment becomes pressurised more than the cabin
The cargo compartment is separated from the cabin ventilation system, so its air is not shared
The cargo compartment receives more hot air
The packs stop

explanation: Isolation valves let the cargo compartment ventilation be isolated from the rest, for instance in a smoke procedure.

question: What happens to the ventilation of the forward cargo compartment during the cargo smoke procedure?

options.text: The compartment is connected to the cabin to remove the smoke
The compartment's extract fan runs faster
Its ventilation is isolated, so smoke is not spread to the rest of the aircraft
The compartment is pressurised

explanation: The aim of the procedure is to contain the smoke and fire so that it does not spread; isolating the ventilation is the first of those steps.

question: Which pushbutton isolates the cargo compartment ventilation, and how is it indicated?

options.text: The ISOL VALVES pushbuttons on the cargo ventilation panel, with an OFF light
The DITCHING pushbutton
The RAM AIR pushbutton
The MODE SEL selector

explanation: Cargo ventilation is controlled from a dedicated panel, where each isolation valve and extract fan has its own switch.

question: What is the source of air for the avionics ventilation system in the open circuit configuration?

options.text: Air from the cabin, which is then extracted overboard
Air from the engine bleed
Air from the cargo hold
Fuel tank vent air

explanation: In open circuit the air is drawn in, passes through the equipment and goes directly overboard, with no recirculation. It is used when cooling needs are high on the ground.

question: In which situation is the avionics ventilation closed circuit configuration typically used?

options.text: During engine start only
On the ground on a hot day
In flight, when the fuselage skin is cold enough to cool the air
Only when the APU is running

explanation: The skin is cooled by the outside air in flight, so recirculating avionics air against it is efficient and uses no cabin air.

question: What does the ECAM show in the event of an avionics ventilation fault?

options.text: A warning with a master warning light only
A caution message with the affected fan or the system, such as BLOWER FAULT or EXTRACT FAULT
No message, only an overhead light
A memo message in green

explanation: Faults of this kind are cautions: an amber message and the master caution, with the relevant light on the panel.

question: What is the primary purpose of the cabin air filters upstream of the recirculation fans?

options.text: To dry the air from the packs
To cool the air from the cabin
To reduce the noise from the fans
To remove dust and contamination from the air before it is recirculated into the mixer unit

explanation: Clean recirculated air keeps the ducts and the mixer unit clean and improves cabin air quality.

question: What does the abbreviation AEVC stand for?

options.text: Air extraction valve controller
Automatic engine ventilation control
Avionics equipment ventilation computer
Avionics electrical voltage converter

explanation: The AEVC runs the avionics ventilation system. Its name tells you what it does: it controls the ventilation of the avionics equipment.
